reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a step-by-step flash-loan arbitrage method that instructs participants to deploy supplied contract code, fund it with BNB, and call a flashloan function for a stated 2.51 BNB gain. It connects the requested transfer and contract operation to claimed repeatable profits, including a statement that larger loans are almost guaranteed to work. Although the speaker calls it educational and notes that earnings vary with liquidity, the video still gives participation instructions alongside a financial-return claim.

citations.quote: How to use Pancakeswap to make money
Copy the Contract code at - https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HYeGG3DdlaxHkP2tiC3QxWmiRlnjUtFNvuC7QxYa_Sc/edit?usp=sharing
Send 0.2 BNB to the contract for gas fee for all swaps
Please note that the transaction sender (Us) gains 2.51 BNB from the arbitrage.
Call 'flashloan' function in Remix.

opening.argument: The material repeatedly qualifies its claims rather than presenting a guaranteed return. It says earnings depend on liquidity, and explains that an unprofitable transaction reverts, limiting the stated downside to network fees. The speaker likewise says outcomes depend on price changes, market conditions, and trading participants. Those are material risk disclosures, not a promise that every viewer will profit. The stated example is therefore best understood as a conditional technical demonstration whose result depends on volatile market conditions, with failure expressly acknowledged.

then the transaction will revert as if nothing happened which is the nature of flash loans.
at the worst case scenario is that we lose some network fees and the best case scenario is as you can see a lot of bmbs
it has to do with the price changes and other metrics it depends on the time of the day it depends on the cost of bn, it depends on the cost of BMP, it depends on the buyer and sellers

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening emphasizes the claimed gain and the instructions, but it omits the explicit qualifications. The cited 2.51 BNB figure is presented as a transaction example, while the material says earnings vary and unsuccessful transactions revert. Calling the content instructional does not by itself establish deceptive solicitation when the same instructions include conditions, costs, and failure scenarios.

citations.quote: The amount you can earn varies and depends on the arbitrary differences in the liquidity of the pool.
then the transaction will revert as if nothing happened which is the nature of flash loans.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warnings do not neutralize the central inducement. The material still instructs viewers to fund a contract and pursue returns, while describing a larger flash loan as nearly certain to work. A reversion may avoid completing the loan, but the cited language does not establish that the required gas, contract, or wallet interactions are risk-free, nor does it independently verify the claimed result.

citations.quote: A flash loan of 5,000 BNB or higher is almost guaranteed to work every time but occasionally lower amounts such as the one demonstrated in the video can work too.
Send 0.2 BNB to the contract for gas fee for all swaps

opening.argument: The content is framed as technical education and a live demonstration of how flash loans and arbitrage operate. The speaker introduces it as part of an educational series, explains the underlying same-transaction repayment principle, and walks through Remix, contract creation, deployment, and execution. The described activity concerns programming and decentralized-finance mechanics, not merely a request to send money to an unnamed recipient. The supplied frames also show a development environment with source code and transaction controls, consistent with an operational demonstration. That context supports classification as educational technology content.

citations.quote: welcome to the second part of the educational series on block chain exploits
this video is for people who wants to get familiar with the nature of the flashnose
this is the website where people code and deploy the smart contracts

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats technical detail as evidence of education while overlooking the demonstrative purpose of the walkthrough. Explaining a tool and showing its deployment can still be instructional technology content; the presence of an execution step does not convert a coding lesson into a deceptive financial offer. The speaker expressly identifies the video as educational and explains the mechanics before the example.

citations.quote: this video is for people who wants to get familiar with the nature of the flashnose
This allows us to use the money to make profit through arbitrage and other opportunities

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling something educational does not determine its practical effect. The material gives viewers a contract source, funding instructions, and a function to call, then links that process to claimed BNB gains. The technical presentation may be genuine, but it remains a participation tutorial whose educational framing does not establish that the financial-return claim is reliable.

opening.argument: The evidence does not show several features that would ordinarily support a scam-mechanism finding. It does not identify a membership fee, downline, credential request, or promise that deposited principal will be returned by a seller. Instead, it describes a user-operated arbitrage contract and separately identifies transaction gas as a network cost. The material also says an unprofitable operation reverts, rather than claiming that a platform will retain a deposit regardless of outcome. At most, this is a technical service-like workflow involving code, a wallet, and blockchain transaction fees.

citations.quote: Send 0.2 BNB to the contract for gas fee for all swaps
then the transaction will revert as if nothing happened which is the nature of flash loans.
unlike the traditional loans we are expected to payback in the same transaction.
This script will create a virtual token so that we can do the operations

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening infers a scam from a blockchain workflow without identifying the missing mechanism. The cited material describes gas for swaps and same-transaction repayment, not a request for credentials, a downline, or a seller-held deposit. A claimed arbitrage outcome may be disputed, but disputability alone does not establish that the ordinary transaction mechanism is fraudulent.

citations.quote: Send 0.2 BNB to the contract for gas fee for all swaps
we are expected to payback in the same transaction

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing categories listed here are not required to show the relevant concern. The material directly tells viewers to copy code, deploy a contract, send BNB to it, and call a function in pursuit of a stated gain. Describing the transfer as gas does not establish that the code or claimed return is trustworthy, and the reversion explanation does not prove the funding step is harmless.
